It is a reminder that spring will always follow winter.
"The land gives of itself. Its abundance provides, even in times of chaos."
"My people blazed these pathways long ago, before the Eldrazi came. We will ride them long after the Eldrazi are gone."
"The most elegant solutions are found in nature. You just have to know where to look."

"Humans use pigs to hunt for mushrooms, don't they? It's like that."
—Harak, Malakir bloodwitch
"My people are no longer slaves to the Eldrazi, beholden to the past. We will determine our own future."
"Before the battle, I heard them take an oath near the ruins of Sea Gate. I hope they inspire others to keep watch."
"Some relic hunters have given up exploring and gone to fight the Eldrazi. But I know our work is more important than ever. The secrets we uncover could lead to the world's salvation."
Greenweaver Mina and her twin brother Denn lead the last of the Mul Daya into an uncertain future.
"I swore to take one head for each member of my family they killed. My task is nowhere near its end."
Roilmages' tactics are as chaotic as the energies they channel.
"When I'm done training you, anything will be a deadly weapon."
Once a simple tool, it—like everything else on Zendikar—has been turned into a weapon against the Eldrazi.
Forged for victory in a time of despair.
Forged for victory in a time of despair.

"If we're going to survive, we have to use every tool at our disposal. Especially the disgusting ones."
—Ryza, Oran-Rief scout

"It's endearing, in a mystical, pointy sort of way."
—General Tazri, allied commander
A light to bring hope in dark times.
The nomadic kor carry only necessities on their long treks. The coming of the Eldrazi redefined "necessities."

"Sometimes being fast is as important as being smart."
—Ryza, Oran-Rief scout
A mudflow swallowed the lowlands years ago. All that remains are a bottomless mire and an endless rain of ash.

"Look, and see the future."
—Ayli, high priest of the Eternal Pilgrims
Even in areas of profound devastation, the hedrons remained intact.
The river split into many channels as it flowed to the Halimar Sea. Few travelers could follow the same one twice.
Once a center for knowledge, Sea Gate now serves as a reminder of what was lost.

"Long after the land has given up the last of its secrets, there will still be mysteries in the depths of the sea."
—Kiora
Tazeem's embrace is harsh, but for those that call it home, nothing else will do.
Despite the chaos of the Roil and the devastation of the Eldrazi, Zendikar is a world of breathtaking beauty.
Kozilek's presence warped the land, stripping away layer after layer.

"Peace will come only when we have taken Varchild's head."
—Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian Chieftain

"We must shake her limbs and rattle her brains."
—Grandmother Sengir
Valuing scholarship above all else, the inhabitants of the Ivory Tower reward those who sacrifice power for knowledge.

"Ach! Hans, run! It's the Lhurgoyf!"
—Saffi Eriksdotter, last words

"Don't look at it! Maybe it'll go away!"
—Ib Halfheart, goblin tactician

"I will go to any length to achieve my goal. Eternal life is worth any sacrifice."
—Zur the Enchanter

Up and down,
over and through,
back around—
the joke's on you.

Up and down,
over and through,
back around—
the joke's on you.
Battle doesn't need a purpose; the battle is its own purpose. You don't ask why a plague spreads or a field burns. Don't ask why I fight.

"Beast. Defiler. The source of all my pain."
—Ihsan's Shade
That which lasts longest serves best.
That which lasts longest serves best.
She had expected death to roar, to thunder, to growl. She did not recognize it when it came hissing to her side.

"Never taunt an embermage, 'What are you going to do about it?'"
—Akin, seasoned askari

"The so-called Barbarians will not respect us for our military might—they will respect us for our honor."
—Lucilde Fiksdotter, Leader of the Order of the White Shield

"The so-called Barbarians will not respect us for our military might—they will respect us for our honor."
—Lucilde Fiksdotter, Leader of the Order of the White Shield

"And the ignorant shall fall to the squirrels."
—*Chip 2:54*

"And the ignorant shall fall to the squirrels."
—*Chip 2:54*

"It blinked, and flower petals fell like tears. Harthar, sensing weakness, attacked—and his blood fell like petals."
—Shesul Fass, faerie bard
Chains of leaping fire and sizzling lightning laid waste the artificers' handiwork, sparing not a single device.

"Just the thing for those pesky water mages."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

"Just the thing for those pesky water mages."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

"It is the way of most wizards to begin by exiling themselves and to end by exiling everyone else."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator

"The raging waters had swept away trees, bridges, and even houses. My healers had much work to do."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

"The raging winds . . . , settling on the sea, the surges sweep, / Raise liquid mountains, and disclose the deep."
—Virgil, *Aeneid, Book I*, trans. Dryden

"Heed the lessons of our time: the forms of water may move the land itself and hold captive the fires within."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran royal mage

"Heed the lessons of our time: the forms of water may move the land itself and hold captive the fires within."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran royal mage
A shield of light admits no shadow.

"Once, our people could call down the storm itself to do our bidding."
—Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian Chieftain

"Leaves more room for the big ones to fight in, you know."
—Jaya Ballard, Task Mage

"Leaves more room for the big ones to fight in, you know."
—Jaya Ballard, Task Mage

"He traded sand for skins, skins for gold, gold for life. In the end, he traded life for sand."
—Afari, *Tales*

"It's filthy work, planting them."
—Kifimbo, Shadow Guildmage

"Wealth is a good thing, compared to poverty—your food is better, your robes are softer, and your companions have bathed more recently."
—Kipkemboi, Kukemssa pirate

"I write upon clean white parchment with a sharp quill and the blood of my students, divining their secrets."
—Shauku, Endbringer

"But I signed nothing!"
—Taraneh, Suq'Ata mage

"Part of me believes that Barrin taught me meditation simply to shut me up."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"Part of me believes that Barrin taught me meditation simply to shut me up."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"I'm too modest a wizard to reveal the full extent of my abilities."
—Ertai, wizard adept

"Dragonfire forged me a warrior."
—Rashida Scalebane

"If you weren't born with it, you don't need it."
—Grahilah, former trader of Amiqat

"If you weren't born with it, you don't need it."
—Grahilah, former trader of Amiqat

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Create a 2/1 green Spider creature token with reach.
II — Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control. It becomes a legendary Spider Hero in addition to its other types.
III — Target creature you control gains double strike until end of turn.

(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Surveil 3.
II — When you next cast a creature spell this turn, copy it, except the copy isn't legendary.
III — Choose a card name. Whenever a creature with the chosen name deals combat damage to a player this turn, draw a card.

(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Destroy target creature.
II — Each player may discard a card. Each player who doesn't loses 3 life.
III — Exile any number of target players' graveyards.

(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Until your next turn, each creature attacks each combat if able and attacks a player other than you if able.
II — Add {R}{R}{R}.
III — This Saga deals 5 damage to each opponent.

(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Mill five cards. When you do, this Saga deals damage equal to the greatest power among creature cards in your graveyard to target creature.
II — Target creature you control gets +2/+2 until end of turn.
III — Return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand.

faces.f: She keeps the festival's revels from faltering, infusing the witches' rituals with hope.

"It is amusing that the fleshlings believe we are at war. In truth, they are nothing but scurrying pests to be eradicated."
—Azax-Azog, the Demon Thane
At Neyali's command, they took position. At Otharri's signal, they struck.

"Funny, I always thought the Phyrexians were a heartless lot."
—Kaya
When the alarm crystals flash, Drannith's finest answer the call.
A righteous sovereign makes for a blessed realm.

"Abandon your selfish ambitions and become one with the Flesh Singularity."
—Elesh Norn
When the earth shudders, the sky overflows.
The sky boiled over the citadel, dire and dark. Then the angels brought the dawn.

"Captain, your units are the tip of our spear. There is zero room for failure."
—Jirina Kudro

"Ghirapur's gremlin population poses a threat to the infrastructure of the fairgrounds. Threats must be eliminated."
—Sram, senior edificer
The best presents are impossible to regift.
Though the spirits' bodies were ethereal, Agnur soon learned that their blades were quite solid—and razor-sharp.
"One faith, but many hands in victory."
First among equals.
Those who are chosen do not doubt. Those who remain do not lament.
In life, they were a motley crew: farmers, lords, cutpurses, priests. In death, they are united in singular, benevolent purpose.
Their war forgotten, the nations of Bant stood united in the face of a common threat.
"In these halls there is no pass or fail. Your true test comes with the first full moon."
The path back to the world of the living is murky and bewildering. A geist may not even realize that it's terrifying its own loved ones.
After his death, the general was reunited with fallen soldiers from over thirty of his campaigns.
As long as one drop of the oil exists, the joyous work continues.
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."
After the Battle of Liet Field, the white sun crested above Taj-Nar, bringing hope to all who survived the carnage.

"Her voice is justice, clear and relentless."
—Akroma, angelic avenger
"I am weak. Make . . . me . . . ideal."

"I have seen things that would reduce a weaker person to blubbering and raving. Want to hear about them?"
—Vraska
As the Eldrazi spread, no secret that could give Zendikar's defenders an advantage was considered too dangerous to seek.
It leaves its victims one sting closer to phyresis.

"We train for the improbable, like lightning striking the same place twice, or striking everywhere at once."
—Nundari, Sea Gate militia captain
"This world will be ruled by its rightful sovereigns, not these hideous pretenders."
Each monstrosity that fails to kill him expands his conjured arsenal.

"Leave no scraps, lest you attract pests."
—Mardu threat
Those with knowledge are wise to listen to those with imagination.
"Ready . . . uh . . . fire!"

"Kill the weak so they can't drag the strong down to their level. This is true compassion."
—Benzir, archdruid of Temple Might
Its venom drips with Phyrexia's hate.
The natural order is out of order.
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
"To care for yourself, cultivate the world. To care for the world, cultivate yourself."

"I wish I could take credit for it, but nature progresses on its own, just the way it should."
—Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger

"Dead or alive, my creations are stronger than Jin-Gitaxias's septic minions."
—Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger
In nature, not a single bone or scrap of flesh goes to waste.
"Your own frailty is your undoing. I am merely the one to expose it."
Cries of anguish quickly spurred cries of action.
"As long as my hand holds a blade, there's hope for a pure Mirrodin once again."

"The heroes of the past nourish our spirits by their example—and nourish our crops by their decay."
—Jeddeg, philosopher of graves

"Your debt is erased."
—Hilgur, Orzhov euthanist

"All matter, animate or not, rots when exposed to time. We merely speed up the process."
—Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer
Torn from history. Torn from memory. Torn from reality.
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.

"Have you ever held a Boros signet? There's a weight to it that belies its size—a weight of strength and of pride."
—Agrus Kos
By guild tradition, any puddle of multicolored light on the cobblestones can serve as neutral ground.
It harmonizes with the essence of its master.

"What do you have that I cannot obtain?"
—Mairsil, the Pretender
Depending on your point of view, the seal represents a proud guardian of the natural cycle or one who has sold her soul to darkness for eternal life.
"Arise, great one, and cleanse the world of our enemies!"

"A crafter must imbue her weapon with part of her soul—something the Phyrexians are incapable of doing."
—Melira

"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?"
—Jhoira, master artificer
They watch for a new master, one more sinister than the last.
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.

"The sun banishes darkness every morning. I too will rise with such assuredness."
—Huatli
It's much easier to list the places they *haven't* been.
History has buried its treasures deep.
The continent of Murasa lies beneath a blanket of dense vegetation, its enormous branches tangled so thickly that some inhabitants never see the ground.
Without Ardenvale's loyalty, the realm would greedily devour itself.
Without Embereth's courage, the realm would falter and fall.

"Approach my tower on bended knee or depart from it as ash upon the wind."
—Gadwick, the Wizened

"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them."
—Pulan, Bant orchardist
A seething locus of reverent rage.

"I can't protect everyone here. But those I can, I will."
—Karn

"I swear, for every one Prossh devours, three more pop out of a hole somewhere."
—Jaya Ballard
A hungry lair of flourishing rot.
That which endures, survives.
A flickering beacon of righteous corruption.
Its courtyards are lit during every hour of the day so that night may never fall within its walls.
On Otaria, peace and harmony are rare. Places that provide both are cherished.

"When gods become apathetic, the people will worship anyone who answers their pleas."
—Kiora
There's never a need to change the watch, for the servants of Norn are sleepless.
"Be not afraid of the holy chorus. Join in rapturous harmony."
"Let those thanebound dissenters prattle about their dead god. I serve the Mother of Machines, and in her name I carve out their heresy."
"Elspeth, my friend, the Multiverse has answered my prayers to bring you here so that I may gather you into my pride and forever protect you."
"We need not be swift. We are inexorable."
"There is no hate behind our blades. We kill out of love, and the desire to share Norn's blessings with all."
"My mother wore this into battle against the first Phyrexians. Now I wear it in her honor."

"You think it's creepy now? You should see how it eats."
—Melira
"I have room for a few more teeth in my collection. Who's next?"
"It's hard to fight for the future if you can't see the way forward."
While one mouth feeds, the other chatters mindless paeans of Elesh Norn's glory.

"Drown, so you may breathe again."
—Atraxa
The mites sniff out any potential interlopers. He handles the rest.
Only Elesh Norn's most loyal servants are granted the honor of becoming part of her throne.

"Behold your inevitable defeat."
—Elesh Norn
New Phyrexia's planar defenses scattered the Planeswalker strike team on arrival. Elesh Norn knew they were coming.

"Witness the glory of true, unwavering unity."
—Ajani
"There is a single, glorious truth, etched in the hearts of the faithful. Join in unity, or be washed away."
"Well, aren't you a sight for sore eyes!" said Koth. "I was about to say the same, my friend," Elspeth replied.
He spreads word of the Argent Etchings to a captive audience.

"It's hard to tell with this glare, but those must be the skyhunter reinforcements! They have arrived at last!"
—Prahan, Mirran rebel
Faced with a blast that would level not only New Phyrexia, but also a dozen innocent worlds, Elspeth consigned it—and herself—to the nothingness in between.

"Hear only harmony. See only glory. Speak only truth."
—Atraxa
For the aspirants of the Progress Engine, being launched into the sphere's upper reaches is a great honor. Some are even granted wings beforehand.
It is Jin-Gitaxias's deepest exasperation that any part of his domain still requires maintenance.

"Where once there was ignorance, Jin-Gitaxias brought knowledge, and an age of progress dawned."
—Monument inscription
Kaya watched in horror as the illusion vanished from her hands. Jace held the real Sylex—and had activated it before phyresis claimed his mind.
It can catch a rat and perform a spinal tap with one graceful swipe of its paw.
"Free will was an illusion so perfect it fooled even me. I know better now."

"Careful—however they might look, they're not human. A step too close and they'll drag you in."
—Kara Vrist, resistance spymaster
One morning, the test subject decided to perform trials on the scientists.

"Drink deeply of the truth, and become *compleat*."
—Tamiyo
An inconsistency in a routine vivisection sparked a revelation about the inner workings of the Orthodoxy's centurions.
Bored with the ruins of Lumengrid, it migrated to the ruins of the Mephidross.
"The oil is all-knowing. The trick is to ask the right questions."
"I've isolated the chirality of the glistening oil, so there will be no wasted precursors."
Each of the Gitaxian sectives watches the others, looking for any hint of imperfection.

"Imagine a giant room, like a library . . . except instead of books, it's filled with body parts."
—Kara Vrist, resistance spymaster
No matter how many times he saw it, Sarnvax always relished the look of dawning horror as his foes realized their mistake.
"Please, for science, tell me how it feels. Leave nothing out."
It no longer needs to eat, but old instincts are put to use ridding the Surgical Bay of spies.

"Your theory holds merit. You do not."
—Sarnvax, Gitaxian sective
"I bring a message from the Autonomous Furn—argh!"
Visitors to the Surgical Bay often become permanent residents.

"We are opening a new chapter in the one true story of Phyrexia. Someone must record it for posterity."
—Tamiyo
"Experimental Log 290: Leaving the subject's pain receptors active appears to yield an unprecedented combination of incoherence and hyperawareness."
After a series of ambushes, Uulbrek demanded a sentry with no blind spots.
The Mirran forces thought they'd vanquished their foes . . . until a nearby monument got up and started stalking toward them.
By gaze, sting, and claw, Vraska will see the will of Phyrexia done.
Many vatkeepers use necrogen etchings to judge the value of their aspirants. If the wounds rot and fester, the recipient is not worth further effort.

"Watch your footing around here. Anything you might step on probably has teeth."
—Kara Vrist, resistance spymaster

"Where once there was complacence, Sheoldred brought ambition, and soon the will of Yawgmoth reigned."
—Monument inscription

"Get away from there! I must rebuild that one for the next bout. Shoo, shoo!"
—Keskit, the Flesh Sculptor
What cannot be remade will be unmade, one scrap at a time.
The gospel of lies sounds sweetest when whispered by many mouths.
"We both serve the Demon Thane. Your parts would better serve with me."
Sinking into the Dross is neither a gentle death nor a quiet one. But once the necrogen takes hold, it is inevitable.

"Give of yourself, for compleation awaits the cleansed."
—Nokar, priest of Sheoldred
They wished to become vital parts of the Dross Pits. Azax-Azog granted their request.
What she lacks in skin she makes up in swagger.
"It seems someone forgot to read the fine print."

"Does anyone else hear that horrible crunching sound?"
—Jace
"I give you pain, you give me information. A simple trade, is it not?"
"Give all you are to Phyrexia, and you will receive more than you could have ever desired."
The praetors of the other Spheres privately wonder how Sheoldred always has a surplus of glistening oil at her disposal.
For a bittersweet moment, Jace believed he could still save his love. A moment was all Vraska needed. "For the glory of Phyrexia," she whispered.

"Show me what Norn's sycophants are hiding under all that pretty porcelain."
—Sheoldred
Some of Sheoldred's goliaths spread the glory of Phyrexia. Others just eat.
"I have raised many of my own contenders for the Coliseum. This one will be fearsome one day, mark my words."
"Congratulations. I am entertained."
The punishment for sedition, like every other crime in the Dross Pits, is execution.
From within its form, a single word echoed forth: "Devour."
She proudly carries the weight of Phyrexia's creed, both figuratively and literally.
The first rebirth is a reward. The fifty-first is a punishment.
"Soon enough each praetor will have hired me to kill the others, and I will stand alone as the true Father of Machines."
The dull, creeping pain of phyresis curdled in Vraska's blood. She knew as soon as it took her, she would betray everything—even Jace.
"Live or die, you serve the Steel Thanes now."
The Invasion Tree broke through the Blind Eternities and sent Phyrexian perfection coursing across the Multiverse.

"Without faith in each other, we truly would have nothing left. Isn't that right, Malach? ...Malach?"
—Darven, Mirran rebel, last words
"I will not rest until the truth of Phyrexia is inscribed across the Multiverse."
"Finally, a safe way to punch the rotters in the face."
"To dance to the music of Juex, leap like the flickering flame and hit like the hammer."

"They call themselves the Quiet Furnace? Ironic."
—Tyvar

"They're violent, headstrong, and wildly unpredictable. It should be amusing to see how Norn's vaunted tactics try to cope with them."
—Urabrask
He finally understood that phyresis was not an ending, but a new, perfect beginning.
She marks her favorite creations with a searing brand, leaving all others to be consumed by the furnace.
With the Quiet Furnace closed to all other factions, Urabrask's smiths were free to build anything their creativity demanded.
Urabrask encourages creativity in all its forms, even the destructive ones. Especially the destructive ones.
The Machine Orthodoxy finds strength in numbers. The Quiet Furnace finds that amusing.

"No matter how tough they are, even Phyrexians prefer to keep their guts on the inside."
—Jor Kadeen
You would laugh too if you just burned through a tyrranax's stomach.
"Perhaps this will show the Orthodoxy what we think of their attempts at indoctrination."
Nahiri's last free breath became a defiant roar as she tore apart Sheoldred's Coliseum.
Popular wisdom says that Phyrexians don't feel fear. But popular wisdom has never tried to hold a bridge against an angry ogre.
"That Great Work of yours is looking pretty fragile, Urabrask!"

"Where once there was apathy, Urabrask brought passion, and the Great Work truly began."
—Monument inscription
When the Vulshok taught him the word for "home," he knew it was what he had been fighting for.
Sometimes the Great Work requires destruction to allow for more efficient reconstruction.

"They may have unlimited mites, but that just means we have unlimited ammunition."
—Urabrask
Once he fought to save Mirrodin. Now he fights to remake it.
As the infection spread, Nahiri's thoughts grew tangled. She needed to protect what she loved from Phyrexia... or maybe only Phyrexia could protect what she loved.
"You were so eager to spy on my work, I assume you'll appreciate a hands-on demonstration."
Her faith burns hot enough to sear away the flesh of the heretic.

"There's a war brewing between Norn and Urabrask. Exploit the chaos, and we can take them both down for good."
—Koth

"Not my style, but it'll get the job done."
—Nahiri
"Eat. Sort. Eat. Sort. Eat."
